# Taxonomy of Grid-Based Logic Puzzles

## Primary Classification by Core Mechanic

---

## 1. LOOP PUZZLES
*The primary objective is to draw a single continuous closed loop*

### 1.1 Unconstrained Path Loop
Puzzles where the loop may travel freely between cells, constrained only by clues

- **Slitherlink** — Loop drawn between dots; numbered cells indicate how many sides are used
- **Masyu** — Loop must pass through all circles; black/white circles impose different turn/straight rules
- **Yajilin** — Loop avoids black cells; arrow-numbers indicate count of black cells in a direction

### 1.2 Directional/Wind-Constrained Loop
Puzzles where the direction of loop travel is governed by special rules

- **Nagareru** — Loop direction enforced by arrow cells; wind cells restrict movement direction
- **Suraromu** — Loop starts/ends at numbered circle; must pass through "Gates" in a specified order

### 1.3 Region-Constrained Loop
Puzzles where the loop's interaction with defined regions is the primary constraint

- **Moon-or-Sun** — Loop passes through each bold-line room once; must alternate between all-moon and all-sun rooms
- **Dotchi-Loop** — Loop passes through white circles; within each bold-line area, all circles are either all straight or all turns; loop avoids black circles

### 1.4 Midpoint/Landmark Loop
Puzzles where specific cells impose geometric constraints on the loop's path

- **Mid-loop** — Black circles must be the exact midpoint of a straight segment of the loop

---

## 2. PATH & CONNECTION PUZZLES
*The objective is to draw lines or paths connecting specific elements, without forming a closed loop*

### 2.1 Island Connection
- **Hashiwokakero** — Connect numbered islands with bridges; bridge count matches island number; all islands form one connected network

### 2.2 Pair Connection
- **Numberlink** — Connect matching numbered pairs with non-crossing, non-branching lines that fill or traverse the grid

### 2.3 Sequential Path Placement
- **Hebi** — Place snake segments numbered 1–5 sequentially in white cells; snakes cannot touch; directional visibility rules apply

---

## 3. REGION DIVISION PUZZLES
*The objective is to partition the grid into regions according to specified rules*

### 3.1 Rectangular Region Division
- **Shikaku** — Divide grid into rectangles; each rectangle contains exactly one number equal to its cell count

### 3.2 Polyomino / Fixed-Shape Region Division
- **LITS** — Color one tetromino per bold-line area; same-shaped tetrominoes cannot touch; colored cells form one connected group; no 2×2 squares
- **Five Cells** — Divide grid into pentominoes (exactly 5 cells each); numbered cells indicate how many block-border lines surround them
- **Sashigane** — Divide grid into L-shaped blocks; circles mark the bend; arrows mark one end pointing toward the bend
- **Fillomino** — Fill grid with numbered regions; each region's size matches its number; same-sized regions cannot touch

### 3.3 Paired/Symmetric Region Division
- **Double Choco** — Divide into blocks each containing a white area and a gray area of identical shape; numbers indicate cell count of one color in the block

### 3.4 Movement-Based Region Assignment
- **Satogaeri** — Move circles into bold-line "countries" so each country has exactly one circle; numbered circles move that many cells; paths cannot cross

---

## 4. CELL-SHADING / PAINTING PUZZLES
*The objective is to determine which cells should be colored/filled black*

### 4.1 Shading with Connectivity Constraints
- **Nurikabe** — Shade cells to form a connected black "wall"; numbered white islands must be exactly that size; no 2×2 black squares
- **Heyawake** — Shade cells in bold-line rooms; numbered rooms have exact black cell counts; black cells cannot connect; white cells cannot span more than two rooms in a line
- **Hitori** — Shade cells so each number appears once per row/column; black cells cannot touch; white cells stay connected
- **Kurodoko** — Shade cells so numbered white cells can see exactly that many white cells in all four directions; black cells cannot touch

### 4.2 Shading with Shape Constraints
- **Choco Banana** — Shade rectangular/square groups (black) and non-rectangular/square groups (white); numbers indicate area size
- **Usowan** — Shade cells; numbers indicate adjacent black cell count, but exactly one number per bold-line room is intentionally wrong; black cells cannot connect; white cells stay connected
- **Kurotto** — Shade cells; circled numbers indicate the total count of connected black cells extending from the circle in four directions

### 4.3 Shading with Gravity/Physical Constraint
- **Sto-stone** — Shade cells within rooms per room number; when all shaded cells are "dropped" downward, they must fill the bottom half of the grid exactly

### 4.4 Shading with Tile/Area Uniformity
- **Tilepaint** — Bold-line "tiles" must be entirely shaded or entirely unshaded; diagonal-number cells indicate black cell count in their row/column segment; solution outlines a recognizable object
- **Nuritwin** — Each bold-line region contains exactly two same-sized blocks of shaded cells; all shaded cells connect globally; blocks within a region do not touch; no 2×2 shading

### 4.5 Partial/Triangle Shading
- **Shakashaka** — Place triangular half-cell shadings so remaining white areas always form rectangles/squares; numbers indicate adjacent triangle count

---

## 5. NUMBER/SYMBOL PLACEMENT PUZZLES
*The objective is to place numbers or symbols into cells according to logical constraints*

### 5.1 Unique Number Placement (Sudoku-family)
- **Sudoku** — Place 1–9 in each cell; each row, column, and 3×3 box contains all digits once

### 5.2 Region-Bounded Number Placement
- **Ripple Effect** — Fill rooms with 1–N (N = room size); duplicate numbers in the same row/column must be separated by at least that number of cells
- **Makaro** — Fill rooms with 1–N; arrow-black cells indicate which adjacent cell holds the largest number; same numbers in different rooms cannot be adjacent

### 5.3 Crossword-Style Number Placement
- **Nansuke** — Fill grid (crossword layout) with multi-digit numbers from a provided list; each cell holds one digit

### 5.4 Symbol Fill
- **Juosan** — Fill every cell with — or |; bold-line territories have number constraints on the difference between the two symbols; — cannot stack more than 2 vertically; | cannot stack more than 2 horizontally

---

## 6. BLOCK / DOMINO PLACEMENT PUZZLES
*The objective is to place discrete pieces or blocks onto the grid*

### 6.1 Block Pair Placement
- **Norinori** — Place 1×2 dominoes (pairs of black cells) so each bold-line area contains exactly two black cells; dominoes may cross region boundaries

### 6.2 Sequential/Evolving Block Placement
- **Evolomino** — Place squares in white cells forming blocks; each block contains one pre-drawn arrow; blocks along an arrow's path grow by one cell each step without rotation or flipping

### 6.3 Block Chaining with Shape Uniqueness
- **Chained Block** — Fill cells to create black "blocks"; blocks touch only at corners forming "chains"; each chain cannot repeat a block of the same size and shape (including rotations/reflections); each block contains exactly one number or "?"

---

## 7. LIGHT / VISIBILITY PUZZLES
*The objective is to place elements whose influence radiates outward in straight lines*

- **Akari** — Place light bulbs in white cells; numbered black cells indicate adjacent bulb count; every white cell must be illuminated; bulbs cannot illuminate each other

---

## 8. MAZE / ROUTING PUZZLES
*The objective is to create or navigate a maze structure*

- **Nurimeizu** — Paint bold-line rooms entirely black or white to create a maze from S to G; circle cells lie on the shortest path; triangle cells do not; no 2×2 uniformity; white cells cannot form loops or be isolated

---

## 9. MOVEMENT / ARROW PUZZLES
*The objective is to move objects from their starting positions to target locations*

### 9.1 Circle Movement to Targets
- **Yosenabe** — Move numbered circles horizontally or vertically into gray areas; gray area numbers must equal the sum of entering circles; arrows show movement and cannot cross

### 9.2 Promontory / Directional White-Cell Puzzles
- **Nurimisaki** — Shade cells so circled "promontory" cells each have exactly one white neighbor; numbers in circles indicate length of white line extending from them; white cells stay connected; no 2×2 uniformity

---

## 10. LINE / PENCIL DRAWING PUZZLES
*The objective is to draw non-loop lines or paths from defined starting points*

- **Pencils** — Identify pencil shapes (straight groups of cells with a tip); draw lines from each tip; line length matches the number in the pencil; lines cannot cross or branch

---

## Cross-Classification Summary Table

| Category | Puzzles |
|---|---|
| Loop Puzzles | Slitherlink, Masyu, Yajilin, Nagareru, Suraromu, Moon-or-Sun, Dotchi-Loop, Mid-loop |
| Path & Connection | Hashiwokakero, Numberlink, Hebi |
| Region Division | Shikaku, LITS, Five Cells, Sashigane, Fillomino, Double Choco, Satogaeri |
| Cell Shading | Nurikabe, Heyawake, Hitori, Kurodoko, Choco Banana, Usowan, Kurotto, Sto-stone, Tilepaint, Nuritwin, Shakashaka |
| Number/Symbol Placement | Sudoku, Ripple Effect, Makaro, Nansuke, Juosan |
| Block/Domino Placement | Norinori, Evolomino, Chained Block |
| Light/Visibility | Akari |
| Maze/Routing | Nurimeizu |
| Movement/Arrow | Yosenabe, Nurimisaki |
| Line Drawing | Pencils |
